48	/**
49	 * Recipe for the product-card organism (ui-kits/organisms/zimmProductCard) — composes
50	 * ZimmProductCardMedia (Step 4) and ZimmProductCardContent (Step 5) with no styling of its own
51	 * for either child. This recipe's entire job is the cross-component concerns neither child can
52	 * own by itself:
53	 *
54	 *   1. THE STRETCHED-LINK OVERLAY. ZimmProductCardContent's `nameLink` renders the one real `<a>`
55	 *      in the whole composed tree. Its `::after` is stretched to `inset: 0` against THIS
56	 *      component's own `root` — the nearest positioned ancestor. Confirmed by reading
57	 *      `zimmProductCardContent.css.ts` directly: neither its `root` nor `nameRow`, `nameLink`, or
58	 *      any other part sets `position` anywhere in that file, so nothing between the `<a>` and
59	 *      this `root` intercepts the containing-block chain. (`ZimmProductCardMedia`'s own `root`
60	 *      IS `position: relative`, but Media is a *sibling* of Content under this organism's root,
61	 *      never an ancestor of Content's `<a>`, so it has no bearing on this chain.)
62	 *   2. LIFTING EVERY OTHER INTERACTIVE CONTROL above that overlay — a z-index higher than the
63	 *      overlay's own (left unset), or the invisible overlay would intercept their clicks first.
64	 *      Four separate, single-selector keys rather than one comma-joined selector: verified via
65	 *      this project's own installed Stylis (v4.2.0 — the same engine Emotion/Chakra invoke at
66	 *      runtime, confirmed by direct compilation) that a comma-separated list DOES distribute this
67	 *      recipe's generated class across every branch correctly, but four plain keys need no such
68	 *      verification to trust at a glance and are each individually addressable from a test. Only
69	 *      ONE of the four (`content` buttons) also adds `position: relative` — that element is
70	 *      `position: static` by default in its own component recipe, so a positioned ancestor is
71	 *      needed for z-index to apply at all. `close`, `carousel`, and `media` are the three
72	 *      exceptions: `ZimmProductCardMedia`'s own recipe already positions each of them directly
73	 *      (`close` via `position: absolute, top: 0, right: 0`; `carousel` via `position: absolute,
74	 *      top: 50%, ...`; `media` — its own root — via `position: relative`), so each needs (and
75	 *      gets) only the z-index bump here:
76	 *        - `close` — a competing `position` value previously declared alongside it had HIGHER
77	 *          specificity than Media's own rule (this rule is a class+attribute descendant selector;
78	 *          Media's is a single class) and silently won the cascade, knocking the remove button out
79	 *          of its pinned top-right corner into normal document flow (Fix 1). See the inline
80	 *          comment at that key below and index.test.tsx's "Fix 1" describe block for the proof.
81	 *        - `carousel` — Fix 3 (found during the manual real-browser check performed after the
82	 *          round-2 Scorer PASS, which explicitly flagged that check as still outstanding, not by
83	 *          any automated pass). The lift rule used to target
84	 *          `'[data-card-slot="carousel"] button'` — the two arrow BUTTONS individually, each given
85	 *          its own `position: relative, zIndex: 1` — identical in shape to the `content button`
86	 *          rule above, and every jsdom test passed. A real click in a real browser still landed on
87	 *          the overlay, not the arrow. Root cause: `ZimmProductCardMedia`'s own `carousel` part
88	 *          sets `transform: translateY(-50%)` (to vertically centre the arrow row against `slide`),
89	 *          and `transform` unconditionally creates a NEW stacking context on that element,
90	 *          regardless of its `position`/`z-index`. That traps each arrow button's `zIndex: 1`
91	 *          *inside* the carousel wrapper's own stacking context — it only wins ordering battles
92	 *          against the *other* arrow button, never against anything outside `carousel` (like the
93	 *          content overlay), because the whole `carousel` box is itself just an ordinary
94	 *          z-index:auto participant one level up — and, being earlier in DOM order than
95	 *          `[data-card-slot="content"]`, it lost. Moving the lift to the `carousel` WRAPPER itself
96	 *          (already `position: absolute` from Media's own recipe, so only `zIndex: 1` is needed
97	 *          here, same as `close`) fixes this: the wrapper's own stacking context — not one buried
98	 *          inside it — is what gets compared against the overlay, and it wins outright, carrying
99	 *          both arrow buttons above the overlay with it. This is exactly the gap
100	 *          index.test.tsx's own "KNOWN LIMITATION" docblock warns about — jsdom resolves no
101	 *          stacking contexts at all, so this shipped past every automated check and was only
102	 *          found by a real click in a real browser. See index.test.tsx's "Fix 3" describe block.
103	 *        - `media` — Fix I (SFCC-236, found via a real mobile-device touch-swipe check performed
104	 *          after this branch's own live testing round, not by any automated pass). The media/
105	 *          gallery scroll region itself was never added to this lift list, even though it is
106	 *          exactly as interactive as the controls nested inside it: with no z-index of its own,
107	 *          `[data-card-slot="media"]` sat at the same default/auto stacking layer the overlay
108	 *          itself occupies, so a touch swipe starting on the image landed on the invisible
109	 *          overlay `<a>` first and the real scroll container underneath never received the
110	 *          gesture — the slide indicator still rendered correctly (proving the image data/gallery
111	 *          logic was fine), but nothing paged. Missed earlier because `close`/`carousel`/content-
112	 *          buttons were each checked with a real CLICK (Fix 1, Fix 3 above) — and a click on the
113	 *          image happened to "work" by accident either way, since it also landed on the overlay
114	 *          `<a>` and still navigated to the PDP — so nothing about a plain tap ever surfaced this;
115	 *          only a real SWIPE (which needs the scroll container itself, not the overlay, to be the
116	 *          hit target) exposed the gap. `ZimmProductCardMedia`'s own root is already `position:
117	 *          relative` (its own recipe), so, same as `close`/`carousel`, only the z-index bump is
118	 *          needed here — plus `cursor: 'pointer'`, since this element is no longer inside the
119	 *          `<a>` that used to convey that affordance via the browser's default link cursor. Fixing
120	 *          this the same way used to fix `close`/`carousel` necessarily breaks the accidental
121	 *          click-still-navigates behaviour described above (media no longer lets the click reach
122	 *          the overlay at all) — restored deliberately via a real `onClick` on
123	 *          `ZimmProductCardMedia` instead of relying on the overlay by accident: see index.tsx's
124	 *          own docblock for the click-passthrough narrative, and its `handleMediaClick`, which
125	 *          guards the two arrow buttons and the remove/close button (all real `<button>`
126	 *          descendants of `media`) so they keep doing only their own thing.
127	 *   3. THE HOVER-REVEAL SWAP between price and the PLP/Wishlist size-selector (and Home's
128	 *      hidden-by-default price), gated by the same `(hover: hover) and (pointer: fine)` query
129	 *      `zimmProductCardMedia.css.ts` already uses for its own arrows/indicator split. Each reveal
130	 *      rule fires on `:hover` OR `:has(:focus-visible)` on this same root (Fix 2 rework below,
131	 *      superseded by Fix H — see point 6) — `:hover` alone would leave every reveal permanently
132	 *      unreachable by keyboard on a hover-capable device.
133	 *
134	 *      Fix J (SFCC-236, this fix — full defect + fix write-up lives at the end of point 6):
135	 *      "hidden" and "revealed" are expressed via `position`/`clipPath`, not `display`, at every
136	 *      site in this block. `display: 'none'` used to mean "hidden" here, but `display: none`
137	 *      unconditionally strips an element from the accessibility tree, not just from paint — see
138	 *      point 6's own Fix J note for the full defect this caused. Hidden is now `position:
139	 *      'absolute', clipPath: 'inset(50%)'` (out of flow, paints nothing — identical visual/layout
140	 *      footprint to `display: none` — but stays in the DOM, tab order, and accessibility tree);
141	 *      revealed is `position: 'static', clipPath: 'none'` (back in normal flow, painted again) —
142	 *      the exact technique `zimmColourSwatchGroup/index.tsx` already ships for its own off-page
143	 *      swatches. The trigger selectors themselves (`:hover`, `:has(:focus-visible)`) are
144	 *      byte-for-byte unchanged by Fix J — only the property values inside these blocks changed.
145	 *   4. NOTIFY-ME'S HOVER GATE (Fix C, found during the SFCC-236 Step 6 visual audit against the
146	 *      real Figma Default+Hover Unavailable instances for all three variations, desktop AND
147	 *      mobile). Three behaviours confirmed together, all different from point 3 above:
148	 *        - `isUnavailable` suppresses the PLP/Wishlist size-selector swap entirely (index.tsx
149	 *          AND-s `hoverHidesPrice`/`hoverRevealsSizeSelector` with `!isUnavailable` before they
150	 *          ever reach this recipe) — there is nothing to pick for an out-of-stock item, so price
151	 *          stays visible on hover instead of being replaced. Home's own `hoverRevealsPrice` is
152	 *          untouched by this — its Unavailable Hover reference still reveals price normally.
153	 *        - Suppressing that swap is not, by itself, enough to reproduce the reference: with no
154	 *          hide/reveal pair of its own, the size-chip wrapper falls back to Content's natural
155	 *          (visible) default and would show permanently — briefly shipped exactly that way mid-fix
156	 *          and caught by re-checking the real render against Figma, which shows size chips hidden
157	 *          in BOTH states when unavailable, not merely "not swapped in on hover". `sizeSelectorUnavailable`
158	 *          (index.tsx: `config.hoverRevealsSizeSelector && isUnavailable`) carries that permanent
159	 *          hide as its own unconditional rule below — deliberately outside `HOVER_CAPABLE_QUERY`
160	 *          entirely, since unlike everything else here this isn't a pointer-type distinction at
161	 *          all: every device sees it hidden, full stop.
162	 *        - Notify-me itself is hover-gated the OPPOSITE way round from price/the size-selector:
163	 *          hidden by default and revealed on hover **only inside `HOVER_CAPABLE_QUERY`**, not
164	 *          unconditionally. Every Desktop Unavailable+Hover reference shows it appearing only on
165	 *          hover; every Mobile Unavailable reference (Mobile has no Hover variant at all, so
166	 *          whatever it shows is the only state a touch pointer ever sees) shows it plainly with no
167	 *          reveal needed. Putting the "hidden by default" half outside the media query — matching
168	 *          point 3's own structure literally — would have made notify-me permanently invisible on
169	 *          touch, since a touch pointer never matches `HOVER_CAPABLE_QUERY` and so could never
170	 *          trigger the `:hover`/`:has(:focus-visible)` half either.
171	 *   5. THE BAG ICON'S PLP-ONLY MOBILE HIDE (Fix D, same SFCC-236 Step 6 visual audit). A genuinely
172	 *      different axis from points 3-4 above: `DESKTOP_QUERY` is a **viewport-width** media query
173	 *      (`min-width`), not `HOVER_CAPABLE_QUERY`'s pointer-capability one — a large touch tablet and
174	 *      a small hover-capable laptop window need to agree with Figma's own Desktop/Mobile split by
175	 *      width, not by input method. Figma's PLP/PDP Mobile Card-content instance
176	 *      (`40002163:41479`) has the bag icon's `Icons` frame `hidden="true"`; Desktop's own PLP
177	 *      instance and Wishlist's Mobile instance (`40002187:58472`) both leave it visible — so this
178	 *      is `hideBagOnMobile`, one boolean `index.tsx` derives from TWO separate per-variation
179	 *      config fields (`hideBagOnMobile` proper, PLP's own unconditional rule; and
180	 *      `hideBagOnMobileWhenUnavailable`, Fix G's narrower Wishlist-only-when-out-of-stock rule —
181	 *      see index.tsx's own docblock and `bagHiddenOnMobile` derivation), not a blanket rule. This
182	 *      recipe only ever sees the one already-combined boolean — it has no opinion on which of the
183	 *      two reasons produced it. Hidden unconditionally by default (mobile-first, matching
184	 *      `zimmProductCardContent.css.ts`'s own padding step direction), then shown again from
185	 *      `DESKTOP_QUERY` up as `display: 'flex'` — not `'block'` — since that is the actual display
186	 *      type `bagWrapper`'s own recipe uses for its icon-centring; this selector's specificity
187	 *      (a class + two attribute selectors) beats Content's single class either way, so restoring
188	 *      the wrong display value would have silently flattened that centring rather than merely
189	 *      failing to apply — the inverse of point 3's hover-reveal shape, but the same "start from
190	 *      the narrowest/most restrictive case, widen from there" idea.
191	 *   6. THE CAROUSEL ARROW REVEAL (behavioural fix, confirmed against the Jira AC — "when on
192	 *      desktop and the user hovers, then the arrows appear" — and live Figma: the Carousel
193	 *      element is `hidden="true"` on every Default-state instance checked and visible only on
194	 *      the matching Hover-state instance, for both PLP and Wishlist). Unlike points 3-4 above,
195	 *      this reveal is **unconditional** inside `HOVER_CAPABLE_QUERY` — not gated behind a
196	 *      `ZimmProductCardStyleProps` flag — because the arrows behave identically across every
197	 *      variation (Home/PLP/Wishlist) whenever a card has more than one image; there is no
198	 *      `VARIATION_CONFIG` entry for it and this fix does not add one. `ZimmProductCardMedia`'s
199	 *      own `carousel` part used to reveal itself unconditionally inside its own
200	 *      `[HOVER_CAPABLE_QUERY]` block — a device-CAPABILITY check, not an actual-hover check —
201	 *      which made the arrows visible permanently on any hover-capable device instead of only
202	 *      while genuinely hovering/focusing the card. That sub-block is now removed entirely from
203	 *      `zimmProductCardMedia.css.ts`; the `:hover`/`:has(:focus-visible)` pair here is the only
204	 *      reveal path left, the same mechanism point 3 already established for price/the size-selector.
205	 *      Purely additive to the existing `carousel` z-index lift in point 2 above — that lift
206	 *      already handles stacking once the arrows are visible; this handles visibility itself.
207	 *
208	 *      Fix H (live-browser check immediately after the above shipped): clicking an arrow button
209	 *      gives it real DOM focus in every evergreen engine, which kept the then-`:focus-within`
210	 *      reveal true — and the arrows visible — even after the mouse moved back out, until focus
211	 *      moved elsewhere entirely (confirmed live: arrows stayed up until a click landed outside
212	 *      the card). The same shared-root `:focus-within` shape underlies every reveal in point 3
213	 *      too (price, the size-selector, notify-me), so a click on a size chip or the notify-me
214	 *      button reproduces the identical stuck-open symptom — this fix was therefore applied to
215	 *      every `:focus-within` occurrence in this recipe, not just this one. `:has(:focus-visible)`
216	 *      replaces `:focus-within` everywhere in this file: it matches only when the browser's own
217	 *      heuristic says a keyboard focus ring is warranted, which a mouse-click-focused `<button>`
218	 *      never satisfies in any evergreen engine, while genuine Tab navigation still does — so
219	 *      keyboard parity (Fix 2's original reason for adding a focus-based reveal at all) is fully
220	 *      preserved, and the mouse-click case is not. `:has()` is new to this codebase as of this
221	 *      fix; it is fully covered by this project's own browserslist (`iOS >= 17`, `Android >= 14`,
222	 *      `last 4 ChromeAndroid versions`), all far past `:has()`'s 2022/2023 shipping baseline.
223	 *
224	 *      Fix J (SFCC-236, live-testing follow-up to Fix H): Fix H's `:focus-within` ->
225	 *      `:has(:focus-visible)` swap above was, and remains, correct for the question it answers —
226	 *      WHEN does a reveal engage — and is not touched by this fix at all, at any of the five
227	 *      sites in this recipe. The defect this fix addresses is a different, previously-conflated
228	 *      question: every one of those five reveals (Home's price, the PLP/Wishlist price<->
229	 *      size-selector swap, notify-me, and this carousel-arrow reveal) used `display` — `none`
230	 *      when hidden, `block`/`flex` when revealed — to answer BOTH "is this painted" and "does
231	 *      this exist for assistive tech" at once. `display: none` unconditionally removes an element
232	 *      from the accessibility tree; it was never a reliable way to answer the second question on
233	 *      its own. `:has(:focus-visible)` is itself a browser heuristic for "does this focus event
234	 *      look keyboard-like," and VoiceOver-driven focus is not guaranteed to satisfy it in every
235	 *      engine — a real, documented mismatch, and not a touch-only concern: `(hover: hover) and
236	 *      (pointer: fine)` is true on any Mac trackpad, so a VoiceOver user on ordinary MacBook
237	 *      hardware is exactly the population this gate applies to. If that heuristic never matches
238	 *      for a given user, all five reveals stayed invisible to them for the entire session,
239	 *      regardless of how they navigated — and because these controls only existed as Tab stops
240	 *      WHILE the interaction condition was true, Shift+Tab entry into the card from something
241	 *      after it used to skip past them entirely (forward-Tab was unaffected: the always-present
242	 *      scroll container triggers the reveal before Tab order reaches the arrows).
243	 *
244	 *      The fix, applied at all five sites: stop using `display` to express "hidden" or
245	 *      "revealed"; use `position`/`clipPath` instead — the exact technique
246	 *      `zimmColourSwatchGroup/index.tsx` already ships for its own off-page swatches. See point
247	 *      3's own rewrite above for the price/size-selector/notify-me detail. Carousel needed one
248	 *      adjustment the other four didn't: this part is `position: 'absolute'` UNCONDITIONALLY
249	 *      already (`zimmProductCardMedia.css.ts`'s own vertical-centring `top: '50%'`/`transform:
250	 *      'translateY(-50%)'`), for a reason that has nothing to do with hiding it — so, unlike
251	 *      price/the size-selector/notify-me, `position` never toggles for carousel at all here (it
252	 *      would have detached `top`/`transform` from having any effect the instant "revealed" set
253	 *      `position: 'static'`, breaking the vertical centring). Only `clipPath` toggles for
254	 *      carousel. Similarly, this recipe's own `&:hover`/`&:has(:focus-visible)` reveal rules for
255	 *      carousel keep their existing `display: 'flex'` alongside the new `clipPath: 'none'` — ADDED
256	 *      to, not replaced by it, unlike every other site in this file. `justifyContent`/
257	 *      `alignItems` on `zimmProductCardMedia.css.ts`'s `carousel` part need `display: flex` to
258	 *      have any effect at all, and once that file's own unconditional `display: 'none'` is gone
259	 *      (replaced by `clipPath: 'inset(50%)'`, with no other rule ever setting `display` for this
260	 *      element outside these two reveal rules), nothing else would ever put the arrows back into
261	 *      a flex row once painted again.
262	 *
263	 *      Two of the five sites' own "hidden" halves needed the identical `position`/`clipPath`
264	 *      correction, not just their paired "revealed" halves: leaving either as `display: 'none'`
265	 *      would not just under-fix the accessibility defect, it would silently DEAD-CODE the paired
266	 *      reveal rule in a real browser — a class of bug this exact file has shipped and fixed once
267	 *      already (see the Fix F+D `[DESKTOP_QUERY]` note in the style object below for the
268	 *      precedent, and `index.test.tsx`'s own "KNOWN LIMITATION" docblock for the analogous jsdom
269	 *      gap). Once a `&:hover`/`&:has(:focus-visible)` rule stops setting `display` at all
270	 *      (replaced by `position`/`clipPath`), a separate, lower-in-the-cascade rule that still sets
271	 *      `display: none` for the SAME property on the SAME element is never overridden by anything
272	 *      — the element stays permanently un-rendered regardless of hover or focus, and every jsdom
273	 *      object-shape test still passes, because each one inspects one recipe key in isolation and
274	 *      never composes both rules through a real cascade the way a browser does:
275	 *        - Home's `hoverRevealsPrice` hidden-by-default rule (inside `HOVER_CAPABLE_QUERY`, per
276	 *          Fix E's own placement) is exactly as much a hover-reveal-gated hidden state as its own
277	 *          `&:hover`/`&:has(:focus-visible)` reveal rules alongside it — it converts too.
278	 *        - `hoverRevealsSizeSelector`'s own hidden-by-default rule (OUTSIDE `HOVER_CAPABLE_QUERY`,
279	 *          "hidden at every breakpoint/pointer type by default") converts as well, for the same
280	 *          cascade reason, even though it sits in a different media-query scope than its own
281	 *          reveal pair. This is NOT the same case as `sizeSelectorUnavailable`'s permanent hide or
282	 *          `hideBagOnMobile`'s mobile hide elsewhere in the style object below — neither of THOSE
283	 *          has any `:hover`/`:has(:focus-visible)` reveal counterpart anywhere in this file at
284	 *          all, so there is no paired rule for either of them to silently dead-code, and both stay
285	 *          exactly as `display: 'none'`/`'flex'`, unconverted, on purpose: separate, correct,
286	 *          Figma-confirmed, non-regressed decisions, not part of the defect this fix addresses.
287	 *
288	 *      **Belt-and-braces addition (carousel only):** `zimmProductCardMedia.css.ts`'s `carousel`
289	 *      part sets `pointerEvents: 'none'` on the wrapper, with `arrowButton` individually
290	 *      re-enabling `pointerEvents: 'auto'` (so a click in the empty centre of the band passes
291	 *      through to the image beneath). While the wrapper was `display: 'none'` by default, that
292	 *      per-button override was harmless — `display: none` removes the entire subtree from
293	 *      hit-testing regardless of any descendant's own `pointerEvents`. Now that the wrapper's
294	 *      hidden state is expressed via `clipPath` instead, its arrow buttons are no longer
295	 *      unconditionally un-hittable purely by virtue of the wrapper being hidden, so this recipe
296	 *      adds an explicit `[data-card-slot="carousel"] button` rule below: `pointerEvents: 'none'`
297	 *      by default (unconditional, alongside the other unconditional lift rules in point 2 above),
298	 *      `'auto'` again only inside the same two revealed selectors — rather than relying on
299	 *      `clipPath`'s own hit-testing suppression alone. Price/the size-selector/notify-me need no
300	 *      equivalent: none of them sets `pointerEvents` anywhere in this file or in
301	 *      `zimmProductCardContent.css.ts`.
302	 *
303	 * Parts: only `root` is declared. Everything above is a nested descendant selector inside
304	 * `root`'s own style object (targeting the composed children's `data-card-slot` attributes), not
305	 * a separate Chakra part — `index.tsx` never reads anything off `useMultiStyleConfig` but
306	 * `styles.root`, so `recipeParts.test.ts`'s declared-vs-read reconciliation needs nothing more.
307	 *
308	 * `zIndex: 1` below is this file's one deliberately unnamed magic number — accepted per
309	 * .claude/rules/conventions.md's own exception ("0, 1, -1 in obvious idiomatic uses"): it is the
310	 * standard "one level above the default/auto stacking layer" value, used identically at each of
311	 * the four lift points, and the stretched-link overlay is deliberately left with no z-index of
312	 * its own rather than pinned to a specific lower number — so the two sides only ever need to be
313	 * *some* value vs a *higher* one, never a specific pair.
314	 */
315	export const ZimmProductCard = {
316	  parts: ['root'],
317	
318	  baseStyle: ({
319	    hoverHidesPrice,
320	    hoverRevealsPrice,
321	    hoverRevealsSizeSelector,
322	    hoverRevealsNotifyMe,
323	    sizeSelectorUnavailable,
324	    hideBagOnMobile,
325	  }: ZimmProductCardStyleProps): Record<string, SystemStyleObject> => ({
326	    root: {
327	      position: 'relative',
328	      width: '100%',
329	
330	      // 1. Stretched-link overlay — see docblock point 1. Deliberately no z-index of its own
331	      // (stays at the default/auto stacking layer), so every control lifted in point 2 below
332	      // reliably paints above it regardless of DOM order.
333	      [`[data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.content}"] a::after`]: {
334	        content: '""',
335	        position: 'absolute',
336	        inset: 0,
337	      },
338	
339	      // 2. Every genuinely-interactive control sits above the stretched overlay. A plain `button`
340	      // type-selector under the relevant data-card-slot root reaches every control uniformly —
341	      // none of them declare their own data-card-slot, and none needs one: Content's bag button,
342	      // its notify-me button, and every ZimmSizeChip button nested inside its own sizeChips
343	      // wrapper are all real <button> descendants of [data-card-slot="content"].
344	      // Fix 1 (Scorer rework round 1): NO position value here. ZimmProductCardMedia's own
345	      // `close` recipe part already sets `position: 'absolute', top: 0, right: 0` on this exact
346	      // element (that's how the remove button pins to the image's top-right corner). This rule's
347	      // `.css-root [data-card-slot="close"]` descendant+attribute selector has HIGHER
348	      // specificity than Media's own single-class rule, so a competing `position` value declared
349	      // here would win the cascade and knock the button out of its pinned position into normal
350	      // flow — which is exactly what shipped here before this fix. The element is already
351	      // positioned (by Media's own recipe), which is all `zIndex` needs to take effect; no
352	      // `position` re-declaration was ever necessary. See index.test.tsx's "Fix 1" describe
353	      // blocks for the object-shape and real-DOM/getComputedStyle proof.
354	      [`[data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.close}"]`]: {
355	        zIndex: 1,
356	      },
357	      // Fix 3 — zIndex only, on the carousel WRAPPER, not on each arrow `button` inside it. See
358	      // docblock point 2 above for why lifting the buttons individually left them unclickable in
359	      // a real browser (a `transform`-induced stacking context on this wrapper trapped their own
360	      // zIndex) despite passing every jsdom test.
361	      [`[data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.carousel}"]`]: {
362	        zIndex: 1,
363	      },
364	      // Fix J — belt-and-braces (see docblock point 6's own Fix J note): the carousel wrapper's
365	      // arrow buttons carry their own `pointerEvents: 'auto'` unconditionally
366	      // (`zimmProductCardMedia.css.ts`'s own `arrowButton` part) — harmless while the wrapper was
367	      // `display: 'none'` by default (that alone removed the whole subtree from hit-testing), but
368	      // no longer guaranteed once the wrapper's hidden state is `clipPath`-based instead (below,
369	      // and in `zimmProductCardMedia.css.ts`'s own `carousel` part). Re-enabled only inside the
370	      // same two revealed selectors, alongside the existing carousel reveal further below.
371	      [`[data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.carousel}"] button`]: {
372	        pointerEvents: 'none',
373	      },
374	      [`[data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.content}"] button`]: {
375	        position: 'relative',
376	        zIndex: 1,
377	      },
378	      // Fix I — the media/gallery scroll region itself, lifted the same way `close`/`carousel`
379	      // already are (docblock point 2's new bullet has the full narrative). `zIndex` is all
380	      // that's needed: ZimmProductCardMedia's own root recipe already sets `position: 'relative'`.
381	      // `cursor: 'pointer'` is added alongside it — this element is no longer inside the overlay
382	      // `<a>` that used to convey that affordance via the browser's default link cursor, and
383	      // index.tsx's own new `onClick` (see that file's docblock) makes it genuinely clickable
384	      // again.
385	      [`[data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.media}"]`]: {
386	        zIndex: 1,
387	        cursor: 'pointer',
388	      },
389	
390	      // 3. Hover-reveal swap — see docblock point 3. The unconditional (outside-media-query)
391	      // half of each flag below is what makes a touch/no-hover pointer see the *default* state
392	      // permanently: it never matches HOVER_CAPABLE_QUERY at all, so whichever rule fired outside
393	      // it (or the total absence of one) is the only state that pointer type ever sees.
394	      //
395	      // `hoverRevealsPrice` (Home) is deliberately NOT here, unlike `hoverRevealsSizeSelector`
396	      // below it — see Fix E in the [HOVER_CAPABLE_QUERY] block: Home's price must stay visible
397	      // unconditionally on a touch pointer, the opposite of what an unconditional hide here would
398	      // do.
399	      ...(hoverRevealsSizeSelector && {
400	        // PLP/Wishlist: size-selector starts hidden at every breakpoint/pointer type. Fix K
401	        // (CodeRabbit finding on PR #85, verified correct before fixing): Fix J converted this to
402	        // `position`/`clipPath` alongside its reveal pair, but this rule is UNCONDITIONAL — unlike
403	        // the other four Fix J sites, whose hidden state only ever applies while a hover-capable
404	        // pointer hasn't revealed the content YET (a state every such pointer can escape), this
405	        // one also applies on a pointer type that can NEVER escape it: `HOVER_CAPABLE_QUERY` never
406	        // matches touch, so there is no reveal path on that pointer type at all (the original,
407	        // Figma-confirmed design — PLP/Wishlist's size picker is a hover-capable-only affordance).
408	        // Keeping this clip-path'd on touch, as Fix J shipped it, left a real `<button>` (each
409	        // `ZimmSizeChip`'s own roving tabindex) permanently in the tab order with no way for that
410	        // pointer type to ever reveal it — reachable by Tab (e.g. a tablet with an external
411	        // keyboard) but invisible and inert forever. Reverted to `display: 'none'` here — the
412	        // hover-capable override, where a reveal genuinely is possible, lives inside
413	        // [HOVER_CAPABLE_QUERY] below instead (see that block's own Fix K note).
414	        [`[data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.content}"] [data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.sizeChips}"]`]: {
415	          display: 'none',
416	        },
417	      }),
418	      // Fix C — see docblock point 4. Unconditional and permanent, on every device: an
419	      // out-of-stock item never gets the size-selector, in any state, so this is the only rule
420	      // for it at all when `sizeSelectorUnavailable` is true (no corresponding reveal exists
421	      // anywhere, inside or outside the media query below). Not part of Fix J's conversion — see
422	      // docblock point 6's own note: this has no reveal counterpart to dead-code, so it correctly
423	      // stays `display: 'none'`.
424	      ...(sizeSelectorUnavailable && {
425	        [`[data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.content}"] [data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.sizeChips}"]`]: { display: 'none' },
426	        // Fix F (full-sweep follow-up audit): mobile-only price hide. Figma's Mobile PLP/Wishlist
427	        // Unavailable references hide price and show notify-me in its place — a genuine swap,
428	        // unlike Desktop's own additive treatment (price stays, notify-me is simply added on
429	        // hover, handled by hoverRevealsNotifyMe below). Hidden by default (mobile-first, matching
430	        // this file's own hideBagOnMobile direction); the DESKTOP_QUERY reveal lives in the single
431	        // shared [DESKTOP_QUERY] block below, NOT a second one here — see that block's own comment
432	        // for why a second `[DESKTOP_QUERY]` object key at this level would silently clobber it.
433	        [`[data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.content}"] [data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.price}"]`]: { display: 'none' },
434	      }),
435	
436	      [HOVER_CAPABLE_QUERY]: {
437	        ...(hoverRevealsPrice && {
438	          // Fix E (full-sweep follow-up audit): the "hidden by default" half moved IN HERE from
439	          // the unconditional block above, where it used to live — Home's Mobile reference
440	          // (40000223:2821) shows price plainly, and Mobile has no Hover variant at all to ever
441	          // reveal a price hidden unconditionally like the original shape did. Confirmed live as
442	          // a real, shipped bug (the Home story showed no price whatsoever at mobile widths), not
443	          // just a Figma reading. Same shape Fix C already established for notify-me, applied
444	          // here for the same underlying reason: a touch pointer must never see this half at all.
445	          // Fix J: was `display: 'none'` — this is the paired hidden state for the two reveal
446	          // rules immediately below and converts along with them (see docblock point 6's own Fix
447	          // J note on why leaving this one as `display: none` would silently dead-code both).
448	          [`[data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.content}"] [data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.price}"]`]: {
449	            position: 'absolute',
450	            clipPath: 'inset(50%)',
451	          },
452	          // ...and is only revealed here, once a hover-capable pointer actually hovers the card.
453	          [`&:hover [data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.content}"] [data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.price}"]`]: {
454	            position: 'static',
455	            clipPath: 'none',
456	          },
457	          // Fix 2 (Scorer rework round 1): `display: none` removes an element from the tab
458	          // order entirely, so a keyboard-only user on a hover-capable device (tabbing, not
459	          // hovering) could never reveal this via `:hover` alone. Originally `:focus-within` on
460	          // this same root — scoped here, not on the price/size-chip wrapper itself, so that

463	          // `_focusWithin` sibling to `_hover`.
464	          // Fix H (live-browser check after the arrow reveal shipped): plain `:focus-within`

471	          // matches when the browser's own focus-visible heuristic says a *keyboard* focus ring

476	          // this project's own browserslist (`iOS >= 17`, `Android >= 14`, `last 4 ChromeAndroid
477	          // versions`), all far past `:has()`'s 2022/2023 shipping baseline. Expressed as a
478	          // separate string key (not a comma-joined `'&:hover, &:has(:focus-visible) ...'`
479	          // selector) to match this file's own established idiom; raw selector strings are used
480	          // throughout rather than a Chakra shorthand prop because the descendant-combinator
481	          // path has to be baked into the selector itself, and Chakra has no `:has()` shorthand.
482	          // Fix J: was `display: 'block'` — converted alongside the `&:hover` entry above; see
483	          // docblock point 3/6 for why `display` no longer expresses this at all.
484	          [`&:has(:focus-visible) [data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.content}"] [data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.price}"]`]: {
485	            position: 'static',
486	            clipPath: 'none',
487	          },
488	        }),
489	        ...(hoverHidesPrice && {
490	          // PLP/Wishlist: price is visible by default (no unconditional rule needed above) and
491	          // hides only here, in favour of the size-selector reveal alongside it. Fix J: both
492	          // entries below were `display: 'none'` — see docblock point 3/6.
493	          [`&:hover [data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.content}"] [data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.price}"]`]: {
494	            position: 'absolute',
495	            clipPath: 'inset(50%)',
496	          },
497	          // Fix 2 / Fix H — see the hoverRevealsPrice block above for the full rationale.
498	          // Keyboard focus anywhere in the card must hide price in favour of the size-selector
499	          // exactly as hover does, so a keyboard user sees the identical revealed state, not a
500	          // different partial one; `:has(:focus-visible)` keeps that true while no longer
501	          // sticking open after a mouse click.
502	          [`&:has(:focus-visible) [data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.content}"] [data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.price}"]`]: {
503	            position: 'absolute',
504	            clipPath: 'inset(50%)',
505	          },
506	        }),
507	        ...(hoverRevealsSizeSelector && {
508	          // Fix K (see the unconditional block above for the full narrative): a hover-capable
509	          // pointer overrides the `display: 'none'` above with the Fix J clip-path technique —

511	          // DOM/tab order while merely not-yet-revealed, for the same VoiceOver/AT reason Fix J
512	          // exists at all. `display: 'flex'` matches ZimmSizeChipGroup's own natural root display

515	          [`[data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.content}"] [data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.sizeChips}"]`]: {
516	            display: 'flex',
517	            position: 'absolute',
518	            clipPath: 'inset(50%)',
519	          },
520	          // ...and is only revealed here, matching the price swap alongside it. Fix J: both
521	          // entries below were `display: 'block'` — see docblock point 3/6.
522	          [`&:hover [data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.content}"] [data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.sizeChips}"]`]: {
523	            position: 'static',
524	            clipPath: 'none',
525	          },
526	          // Fix 2 / Fix H — see the hoverRevealsPrice block above for the full rationale.
527	          [`&:has(:focus-visible) [data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.content}"] [data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.sizeChips}"]`]: {
528	            position: 'static',
529	            clipPath: 'none',
530	          },
531	        }),
532	        // Fix C — see docblock point 4. Both the "hidden by default" declaration AND its reveal
533	        // live inside this same media-query block (unlike price/the size-selector above, whose
534	        // "hidden by default" half is unconditional): a touch pointer never matches this query at
535	        // all, so it never sees the hidden rule below either, leaving notify-me at its natural
536	        // (visible) default — exactly the unconditional visibility every Mobile Unavailable
537	        // reference confirms. Fix J: all three declarations below were `display: 'none'`/

539	        ...(hoverRevealsNotifyMe && {
540	          [`[data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.content}"] [data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.notifyMe}"]`]: {
541	            position: 'absolute',
542	            clipPath: 'inset(50%)',
543	          },
544	          [`&:hover [data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.content}"] [data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.notifyMe}"]`]: {
545	            position: 'static',
546	            clipPath: 'none',
547	          },
548	          // Fix 2 / Fix H — see the hoverRevealsPrice block above for the full rationale.
549	          [`&:has(:focus-visible) [data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.content}"] [data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.notifyMe}"]`]: {

552	          },

569	        // `zimmProductCardMedia.css.ts`'s own unconditional `display: 'none'` is replaced by
570	        // `clipPath`. `position` is deliberately absent from both entries below, also unlike the

573	        // centring the instant the arrows are revealed.
574	        //
575	        // Fix K (CodeRabbit finding on PR #85, verified correct before fixing): a hover-capable
576	        // pointer needs its OWN not-yet-revealed base state here — `zimmProductCardMedia.css.ts`'s
577	        // own `carousel` part reverted to an unconditional `display: 'none'` (Fix K there), which a
578	        // hover-capable pointer must override to `flex`/clipped before `:hover`/`:has(:focus-visible)`
579	        // below can reveal it at all; without this, the arrows never render even on desktop. Touch
580	        // pointers never enter this media query, so they correctly keep the unconditional
581	        // `display: 'none'` and never become tab stops for a control they can never reveal.
582	        [`[data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.carousel}"]`]: {
583	          display: 'flex',
584	          clipPath: 'inset(50%)',
585	        },
586	        [`&:hover [data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.carousel}"]`]: {
587	          display: 'flex',
588	          clipPath: 'none',
589	        },
590	        // Fix J belt-and-braces (see docblock point 6 and the new lift-adjacent rule in point 2
591	        // above): re-enables the arrow buttons' hit-testing only once genuinely revealed.
592	        [`&:hover [data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.carousel}"] button`]: {
593	          pointerEvents: 'auto',
594	        },
595	        [`&:has(:focus-visible) [data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.carousel}"]`]: {
596	          display: 'flex',
597	          clipPath: 'none',
598	        },
599	        [`&:has(:focus-visible) [data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.carousel}"] button`]: {
600	          pointerEvents: 'auto',
601	        },
602	      },
603	
604	      // 5. PLP-only bag-icon mobile hide — see docblock point 5. A separate, sibling media-query
605	      // key from HOVER_CAPABLE_QUERY above (a viewport-width gate, not a pointer-capability one).
606	      // Mobile-first: hidden by default, shown again from the shared [DESKTOP_QUERY] block below.
607	      ...(hideBagOnMobile && {
608	        [`[data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.content}"] [data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.bag}"]`]: { display: 'none' },
609	      }),
610	
611	      // Fix F+D's shared desktop-reveal block — deliberately ONE `[DESKTOP_QUERY]` object key,
612	      // not two. A first version of this recipe gave `sizeSelectorUnavailable` and
613	      // `hideBagOnMobile` each their OWN separate `...(condition && { [DESKTOP_QUERY]: {...} })`
614	      // spread (mirroring how every other flag in this file gets its own independent spread) —
615	      // which silently broke, because both spreads produce a property with the exact same
616	      // *computed key string* (`'@media (min-width: 48em)'`) on the same `root` object. Object
617	      // spread is a SHALLOW merge: it does not deep-merge two spreads that happen to share a key,
618	      // it just lets whichever spread comes LAST overwrite the earlier one's value entirely. With
619	      // `hideBagOnMobile`'s spread positioned after `sizeSelectorUnavailable`'s in this file, its
620	      // `[DESKTOP_QUERY]` object silently replaced the other's, and the price-reveal-on-desktop
621	      // rule vanished from the actual emitted CSS — confirmed for real via
622	      // `document.styleSheets` in a live browser (price stayed `display: none` at 1280px width
623	      // despite `window.matchMedia('(min-width: 48em)').matches` correctly reporting `true`);
624	      // every jsdom test still passed, because each one only ever sets ONE of the two colliding
625	      // flags at a time, never the realistic combination a genuine unavailable PLP card produces.
626	      // `[HOVER_CAPABLE_QUERY]` above never had this problem because it was always written as a
627	      // single key with every contributing condition spread INSIDE it — this block now follows
628	      // that same shape.
629	      [DESKTOP_QUERY]: {
630	        ...(sizeSelectorUnavailable && {
631	          [`[data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.content}"] [data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.price}"]`]: { display: 'block' },
632	        }),
633	        ...(hideBagOnMobile && {
634	          // 'flex', not 'block': ZimmProductCardContent's own `bagWrapper` part sets
635	          // `display: 'flex'` (it centres the icon inside via alignItems/justifyContent) — this
636	          // organism's `[data-card-slot="content"] [data-card-slot="bag"]` selector has higher
637	          // specificity (a class + two attribute selectors vs. Content's own single class) and
638	          // would win the cascade either way, so restoring the actual display type Content uses
639	          // matters here, not just "anything visible" — 'block' would silently flatten that
640	          // wrapper's centering.
641	          [`[data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.content}"] [data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.bag}"]`]: { display: 'flex' },
642	        }),
643	      },
644	    },
645	  }),
646	};

import type { SystemStyleObject } from '@chakra-ui/react';
import { CARD_SLOT, HOVER_CAPABLE_QUERY, DESKTOP_QUERY } from '../../zimmProductCardShared';

/**
 * Same hover-capable-pointer gate `zimmProductCardMedia.css.ts` already establishes for its own
 * arrows/indicator split — now a shared import from `zimmProductCardShared.ts` rather than each
 * file's own module-private copy, so the two can't silently drift. Governs the price <->
 * size-selector swap below, so both composed children's hover treatments engage together off the
 * exact same media feature, on this shared root.
 */

/**
 * A viewport-width gate, unrelated to `HOVER_CAPABLE_QUERY` above — governs the PLP-only bag-icon
 * mobile hide (Fix D, SFCC-236 Step 6 visual audit) below. Also a shared import from
 * `zimmProductCardShared.ts`, same reasoning as `HOVER_CAPABLE_QUERY` above: this and
 * `zimmProductCardContent.css.ts`'s own `root` padding step both need the identical `min-width`
 * gate, and a module-private copy in each file was exactly the drift risk this extraction removes.
 */

type ZimmProductCardStyleProps = {
  /** Home only — see VARIATION_CONFIG in index.tsx. Price is hidden at every breakpoint/pointer
   *  type by default and only appears once a hover-capable pointer actually hovers the card. */
  hoverRevealsPrice?: boolean;

      // 3. Hover-reveal swap — see docblock point 3. The unconditional (outside-media-query)
      // half of each flag below is what makes a touch/no-hover pointer see the *default* state
      // permanently: it never matches HOVER_CAPABLE_QUERY at all, so whichever rule fired outside
      // it (or the total absence of one) is the only state that pointer type ever sees.
      //
      // `hoverRevealsPrice` (Home) is deliberately NOT here, unlike `hoverRevealsSizeSelector`
      // below it — see Fix E in the [HOVER_CAPABLE_QUERY] block: Home's price must stay visible
      // unconditionally on a touch pointer, the opposite of what an unconditional hide here would
      // do.
      ...(hoverRevealsSizeSelector && {
        // PLP/Wishlist: size-selector starts hidden at every breakpoint/pointer type. Fix K
        // (CodeRabbit finding on PR #85, verified correct before fixing): Fix J converted this to
        // `position`/`clipPath` alongside its reveal pair, but this rule is UNCONDITIONAL — unlike
        // the other four Fix J sites, whose hidden state only ever applies while a hover-capable
        // pointer hasn't revealed the content YET (a state every such pointer can escape), this
        // one also applies on a pointer type that can NEVER escape it: `HOVER_CAPABLE_QUERY` never
        // matches touch, so there is no reveal path on that pointer type at all (the original,
        // Figma-confirmed design — PLP/Wishlist's size picker is a hover-capable-only affordance).
        // Keeping this clip-path'd on touch, as Fix J shipped it, left a real `<button>` (each
        // `ZimmSizeChip`'s own roving tabindex) permanently in the tab order with no way for that
        // pointer type to ever reveal it — reachable by Tab (e.g. a tablet with an external
        // keyboard) but invisible and inert forever. Reverted to `display: 'none'` here — the
        // hover-capable override, where a reveal genuinely is possible, lives inside
        // [HOVER_CAPABLE_QUERY] below instead (see that block's own Fix K note).
        [`[data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.content}"] [data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.sizeChips}"]`]: {
          display: 'none',
        },
      }),
      // Fix C — see docblock point 4. Unconditional and permanent, on every device: an
      // out-of-stock item never gets the size-selector, in any state, so this is the only rule
      // for it at all when `sizeSelectorUnavailable` is true (no corresponding reveal exists
      // anywhere, inside or outside the media query below). Not part of Fix J's conversion — see
      // docblock point 6's own note: this has no reveal counterpart to dead-code, so it correctly
      // stays `display: 'none'`.
      ...(sizeSelectorUnavailable && {
        [`[data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.content}"] [data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.sizeChips}"]`]: { display: 'none' },
        // Fix F (full-sweep follow-up audit): mobile-only price hide. Figma's Mobile PLP/Wishlist
        // Unavailable references hide price and show notify-me in its place — a genuine swap,
        // unlike Desktop's own additive treatment (price stays, notify-me is simply added on
        // hover, handled by hoverRevealsNotifyMe below). Hidden by default (mobile-first, matching
        // this file's own hideBagOnMobile direction); the DESKTOP_QUERY reveal lives in the single
        // shared [DESKTOP_QUERY] block below, NOT a second one here — see that block's own comment
        // for why a second `[DESKTOP_QUERY]` object key at this level would silently clobber it.
        [`[data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.content}"] [data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.price}"]`]: { display: 'none' },
      }),

      [HOVER_CAPABLE_QUERY]: {
        ...(hoverRevealsPrice && {
          // Fix E (full-sweep follow-up audit): the "hidden by default" half moved IN HERE from
          // the unconditional block above, where it used to live — Home's Mobile reference
          // (40000223:2821) shows price plainly, and Mobile has no Hover variant at all to ever
          // reveal a price hidden unconditionally like the original shape did. Confirmed live as
          // a real, shipped bug (the Home story showed no price whatsoever at mobile widths), not
          // just a Figma reading. Same shape Fix C already established for notify-me, applied
          // here for the same underlying reason: a touch pointer must never see this half at all.
          // Fix J: was `display: 'none'` — this is the paired hidden state for the two reveal
          // rules immediately below and converts along with them (see docblock point 6's own Fix
          // J note on why leaving this one as `display: none` would silently dead-code both).
          [`[data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.content}"] [data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.price}"]`]: {
            position: 'absolute',
            clipPath: 'inset(50%)',
          },
          // ...and is only revealed here, once a hover-capable pointer actually hovers the card.
          [`&:hover [data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.content}"] [data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.price}"]`]: {
            position: 'static',
            clipPath: 'none',
          },
          // Fix 2 (Scorer rework round 1): `display: none` removes an element from the tab
          // order entirely, so a keyboard-only user on a hover-capable device (tabbing, not
          // hovering) could never reveal this via `:hover` alone. Originally `:focus-within` on
          // this same root — scoped here, not on the price/size-chip wrapper itself, so that
          // focus landing on ANY descendant control (name link, bag button, size chip) triggers
          // the reveal — mirroring zimmSearchInput.css.ts's container/zimmFormRow's own
          // `_focusWithin` sibling to `_hover`.
          // Fix H (live-browser check after the arrow reveal shipped): plain `:focus-within`
          // does not distinguish a real Tab-focused descendant from one that only has focus
          // because the user *clicked* it with a mouse — most browsers give a `<button>` real
          // DOM focus on click, so clicking any interactive control inside the card (an arrow,
          // a size chip, notify-me) left `:focus-within` true, and therefore every reveal below
          // stuck open, until focus moved elsewhere entirely (e.g. a click outside the card) —
          // moving the mouse back out was not enough. `:has(:focus-visible)` fixes this: it only
          // matches when the browser's own focus-visible heuristic says a *keyboard* focus ring
          // is warranted, which excludes a mouse-click-focused `<button>` in every evergreen
          // engine but still matches genuine Tab navigation — so the keyboard case Fix 2 exists
          // for keeps working, and the mouse-click case that produced the stuck-open bug does
          // not. `:has()` is not used anywhere else in this codebase yet; it is fully covered by
          // this project's own browserslist (`iOS >= 17`, `Android >= 14`, `last 4 ChromeAndroid
          // versions`), all far past `:has()`'s 2022/2023 shipping baseline. Expressed as a
          // separate string key (not a comma-joined `'&:hover, &:has(:focus-visible) ...'`
          // selector) to match this file's own established idiom; raw selector strings are used
          // throughout rather than a Chakra shorthand prop because the descendant-combinator
          // path has to be baked into the selector itself, and Chakra has no `:has()` shorthand.
          // Fix J: was `display: 'block'` — converted alongside the `&:hover` entry above; see
          // docblock point 3/6 for why `display` no longer expresses this at all.
          [`&:has(:focus-visible) [data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.content}"] [data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.price}"]`]: {
            position: 'static',
            clipPath: 'none',
          },
        }),
        ...(hoverHidesPrice && {
          // PLP/Wishlist: price is visible by default (no unconditional rule needed above) and
          // hides only here, in favour of the size-selector reveal alongside it. Fix J: both
          // entries below were `display: 'none'` — see docblock point 3/6.
          [`&:hover [data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.content}"] [data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.price}"]`]: {
            position: 'absolute',
            clipPath: 'inset(50%)',
          },
          // Fix 2 / Fix H — see the hoverRevealsPrice block above for the full rationale.
          // Keyboard focus anywhere in the card must hide price in favour of the size-selector
          // exactly as hover does, so a keyboard user sees the identical revealed state, not a
          // different partial one; `:has(:focus-visible)` keeps that true while no longer
          // sticking open after a mouse click.
          [`&:has(:focus-visible) [data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.content}"] [data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.price}"]`]: {
            position: 'absolute',
            clipPath: 'inset(50%)',
          },
        }),
        ...(hoverRevealsSizeSelector && {
          // Fix K (see the unconditional block above for the full narrative): a hover-capable
          // pointer overrides the `display: 'none'` above with the Fix J clip-path technique —
          // this pointer type genuinely CAN reveal the content below, so it needs to stay in the
          // DOM/tab order while merely not-yet-revealed, for the same VoiceOver/AT reason Fix J
          // exists at all. `display: 'flex'` matches ZimmSizeChipGroup's own natural root display
          // (zimmSizeChipGroup.css.ts's `radiogroup`/`oneSize` parts) — `position`/`clipPath` are
          // the only properties the reveal pair below needs to toggle.
          [`[data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.content}"] [data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.sizeChips}"]`]: {
            display: 'flex',
            position: 'absolute',
            clipPath: 'inset(50%)',
          },
          // ...and is only revealed here, matching the price swap alongside it. Fix J: both
          // entries below were `display: 'block'` — see docblock point 3/6.
          [`&:hover [data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.content}"] [data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.sizeChips}"]`]: {
            position: 'static',
            clipPath: 'none',
          },
          // Fix 2 / Fix H — see the hoverRevealsPrice block above for the full rationale.
          [`&:has(:focus-visible) [data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.content}"] [data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.sizeChips}"]`]: {
            position: 'static',
            clipPath: 'none',
          },
        }),
        // Fix C — see docblock point 4. Both the "hidden by default" declaration AND its reveal
        // live inside this same media-query block (unlike price/the size-selector above, whose
        // "hidden by default" half is unconditional): a touch pointer never matches this query at
        // all, so it never sees the hidden rule below either, leaving notify-me at its natural
        // (visible) default — exactly the unconditional visibility every Mobile Unavailable
        // reference confirms. Fix J: all three declarations below were `display: 'none'`/
        // `'block'` — converted together, same reasoning as the price/size-selector pair above.
        ...(hoverRevealsNotifyMe && {
          [`[data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.content}"] [data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.notifyMe}"]`]: {
            position: 'absolute',
            clipPath: 'inset(50%)',
          },
          [`&:hover [data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.content}"] [data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.notifyMe}"]`]: {
            position: 'static',
            clipPath: 'none',
          },
          // Fix 2 / Fix H — see the hoverRevealsPrice block above for the full rationale.
          [`&:has(:focus-visible) [data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.content}"] [data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.notifyMe}"]`]: {
            position: 'static',
            clipPath: 'none',
          },
        }),

        // 6. Carousel arrow reveal — see docblock point 6. Unconditional (no
        // `ZimmProductCardStyleProps` flag gates it): desktop prev/next arrows behave identically
        // across every variation whenever a card has more than one image. Confirmed against the
        // Jira AC ("when on desktop and the user hovers, then the arrows appear") and live Figma:
        // the Carousel element is `hidden="true"` on every Default-state instance checked, visible
        // only on the matching Hover-state instance, for both PLP and Wishlist.
        // `zimmProductCardMedia.css.ts`'s own `[HOVER_CAPABLE_QUERY]: { display: 'flex' }` used to
        // reveal this permanently on any hover-capable device (a device-capability check, not an
        // actual-hover one) — removed entirely there; this pair is now the only reveal path left,
        // the same `:hover`/`:has(:focus-visible)` shape as the price/size-selector swap above.
        // Fix J: `display: 'flex'` stays here (unlike the other four sites' reveal rules, which
        // drop `display` entirely) — `clipPath: 'none'` is ADDED alongside it, not instead of it.
        // See docblock point 6's own Fix J note for why: this part needs `display: flex` for its
        // own `justifyContent`/`alignItems` layout, and nothing else asserts that once
        // `zimmProductCardMedia.css.ts`'s own unconditional `display: 'none'` is replaced by
        // `clipPath`. `position` is deliberately absent from both entries below, also unlike the
        // other four sites: this part is `position: 'absolute'` unconditionally already (Media's
        // own vertical-centring rule), and toggling it to `'static'` here would break that
        // centring the instant the arrows are revealed.
        //
        // Fix K (CodeRabbit finding on PR #85, verified correct before fixing): a hover-capable
        // pointer needs its OWN not-yet-revealed base state here — `zimmProductCardMedia.css.ts`'s
        // own `carousel` part reverted to an unconditional `display: 'none'` (Fix K there), which a
        // hover-capable pointer must override to `flex`/clipped before `:hover`/`:has(:focus-visible)`
        // below can reveal it at all; without this, the arrows never render even on desktop. Touch
        // pointers never enter this media query, so they correctly keep the unconditional
        // `display: 'none'` and never become tab stops for a control they can never reveal.
        [`[data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.carousel}"]`]: {
          display: 'flex',
          clipPath: 'inset(50%)',
        },
        [`&:hover [data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.carousel}"]`]: {
          display: 'flex',
          clipPath: 'none',
        },
        // Fix J belt-and-braces (see docblock point 6 and the new lift-adjacent rule in point 2
        // above): re-enables the arrow buttons' hit-testing only once genuinely revealed.
        [`&:hover [data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.carousel}"] button`]: {
          pointerEvents: 'auto',
        },
        [`&:has(:focus-visible) [data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.carousel}"]`]: {
          display: 'flex',
          clipPath: 'none',
        },
        [`&:has(:focus-visible) [data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.carousel}"] button`]: {
          pointerEvents: 'auto',
        },
      },

      // 5. PLP-only bag-icon mobile hide — see docblock point 5. A separate, sibling media-query
      // key from HOVER_CAPABLE_QUERY above (a viewport-width gate, not a pointer-capability one).
      // Mobile-first: hidden by default, shown again from the shared [DESKTOP_QUERY] block below.
      ...(hideBagOnMobile && {
        [`[data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.content}"] [data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.bag}"]`]: { display: 'none' },
      }),

      // Fix F+D's shared desktop-reveal block — deliberately ONE `[DESKTOP_QUERY]` object key,
      // not two. A first version of this recipe gave `sizeSelectorUnavailable` and
      // `hideBagOnMobile` each their OWN separate `...(condition && { [DESKTOP_QUERY]: {...} })`
      // spread (mirroring how every other flag in this file gets its own independent spread) —
      // which silently broke, because both spreads produce a property with the exact same
      // *computed key string* (`'@media (min-width: 48em)'`) on the same `root` object. Object
      // spread is a SHALLOW merge: it does not deep-merge two spreads that happen to share a key,
      // it just lets whichever spread comes LAST overwrite the earlier one's value entirely. With
      // `hideBagOnMobile`'s spread positioned after `sizeSelectorUnavailable`'s in this file, its
      // `[DESKTOP_QUERY]` object silently replaced the other's, and the price-reveal-on-desktop
      // rule vanished from the actual emitted CSS — confirmed for real via
      // `document.styleSheets` in a live browser (price stayed `display: none` at 1280px width
      // despite `window.matchMedia('(min-width: 48em)').matches` correctly reporting `true`);
      // every jsdom test still passed, because each one only ever sets ONE of the two colliding
      // flags at a time, never the realistic combination a genuine unavailable PLP card produces.
      // `[HOVER_CAPABLE_QUERY]` above never had this problem because it was always written as a
      // single key with every contributing condition spread INSIDE it — this block now follows
      // that same shape.
      [DESKTOP_QUERY]: {
        ...(sizeSelectorUnavailable && {
          [`[data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.content}"] [data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.price}"]`]: { display: 'block' },
        }),
        ...(hideBagOnMobile && {
          // 'flex', not 'block': ZimmProductCardContent's own `bagWrapper` part sets
          // `display: 'flex'` (it centres the icon inside via alignItems/justifyContent) — this
          // organism's `[data-card-slot="content"] [data-card-slot="bag"]` selector has higher
          // specificity (a class + two attribute selectors vs. Content's own single class) and
          // would win the cascade either way, so restoring the actual display type Content uses
          // matters here, not just "anything visible" — 'block' would silently flatten that
          // wrapper's centering.
          [`[data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.content}"] [data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.bag}"]`]: { display: 'flex' },
        }),
      },
    },
  }),
};

141	 * Molecule — the product-card text-content block: heading/link, bag action, wishlist-only
142	 * colour/size attributes, price, PLP-only size-chip picker, and an out-of-stock notify-me CTA.
143	 * Figma "Card-content" component set, node 40002109:26908 (Desktop 40002109:26906 / Mobile
144	 * 40002163:37103).
145	 *
146	 * Deliberately has NO remove/close button — that action lives entirely in
147	 * `ZimmProductCardMedia`'s own `close` overlay (Step 4), positioned on the image, not here.
148	 *
149	 * Also deliberately has no badge slot, despite the SFCC-236 AC mentioning one for PLP/Wishlist.
150	 * An earlier revision of this paragraph claimed no Figma design existed for it at all — that
151	 * was wrong: the badge (Figma "Tag") does exist, confirmed present and identical across every
152	 * Size/Type variant checked. It just lives inside "Image Group", which is
153	 * `ZimmProductCardMedia`'s domain, not this component's — so it was built there instead. See
154	 * that component's own docblock for the confirmed spec, and the organism's own docblock
155	 * ("Badge" note) for which variations actually show it.
156	 *
157	 * Composes `ZimmProductPrice` with `isLive={false}` unconditionally — this is the entire reason
158	 * that prop exists (SFCC-236 Step 3): a grid of these on a PLP must not mount dozens of
159	 * `aria-live` regions whose price never changes post-mount.
160	 */
161	export const ZimmProductCardContent = ({
162	  name,
163	  headingLevel,
164	  href,
165	  currentPrice,
166	  originalPrice,
167	  isPriceLoading,
168	  showAttributes,
169	  colour,
170	  size,
171	  showBag,
172	  isUnavailable,
173	  onAddToBag,
174	  showSizeChips,
175	  sizeChipValues,
176	  selectedSizeChipValue,
177	  onSizeChipSelect,
178	  showNotifyMe,
179	  onNotifyMe,
180	}: ZimmProductCardContentProps) => {
181	  const intl = useIntl();
182	  // `disabled`, not `isUnavailable` — matches `recipeGuards.test.ts`'s own `DEFAULT_STYLE_PROPS`
183	  // key so that guard's exhaustive prop-combination walk actually exercises both the true and
184	  // false branch of `bagButton`'s disabled styling (see zimmProductCardContent.css.ts's own
185	  // comment, and `zimmSizeChip.css.ts`'s identical `disabled` naming for the same reason).
186	  const styles = useMultiStyleConfig(ZIMM_PRODUCT_CARD_CONTENT_RECIPE, { disabled: isUnavailable });
187	
188	  // Was `showNotifyMe && Boolean(onNotifyMe)` — changed 2026-09-08, Marcel's explicit decision.
189	  // The real Notify Me feature (PRD-018–021: a slide-out form submitting to a back-in-stock
190	  // capture target) doesn't exist anywhere in this codebase yet, including on PDP where this
191	  // same prop concept already exists unused — building it is its own future story, not this
192	  // change. Until then, the button ships visible and genuinely inert: `onClick={onNotifyMe}`
193	  // below is a plain prop reference, and `onNotifyMe` stays optional on this component's own
194	  // props — React treats an `undefined` event handler as "no handler attached" (not an error),
195	  // so a click with none supplied safely does nothing.
196	  const showNotifyMeButton = showNotifyMe;
197	
198	  // Figma renders the colour/size attributes line as ONE continuous phrase, not two independent
199	  // labels: the comma is baked into the colour text node's own content ("Lilac Sand,"), not a
200	  // separate punctuation element — confirmed via get_design_context on node 40002187:58446 (the
201	  // real Wishlist Card-content instance). Reproduced the same way here, on the colour value's own
202	  // rendered string (never as a static comma JSX node between the two spans), paired with
203	  // attributesRow's 2px gap (zimmProductCardContent.css.ts) for the "Ivory, M" breathing room —
204	  // verified by rendering the real Futura Round Medium caption style at actual size: the glyph
205	  // ink-to-ink gap the 2px flex gap produces here reads as a genuine (if slightly tighter than
206	  // full-prose) space, not as "Ivory,M" touching. Guarded against `colour` being falsy so a
207	  // caller omitting it (a contract violation, but not this component's job to enforce) still
208	  // renders nothing, rather than the literal string "undefined,".
209	  const colourWithComma = colour ? `${colour},` : colour;
210	
211	  return (
212	    <chakra.div __css={styles.root} data-card-slot={CARD_SLOT.content}>
213	      <chakra.div __css={styles.nameRow}>
214	        <ProductNameLink to={href} __css={styles.nameLink}>
215	          <ZimmProductName name={name} as={headingLevel} />
216	        </ProductNameLink>
217	
218	        {showBag && (
219	          <chakra.div __css={styles.bagWrapper} data-card-slot={CARD_SLOT.bag}>
220	            <chakra.button
221	              type="button"
222	              __css={styles.bagButton}
223	              aria-label={intl.formatMessage(messages.addToBag)}
224	              disabled={isUnavailable}
225	              onClick={() => {
226	                // Belt-and-braces: the native `disabled` attribute already prevents the browser
227	                // from ever dispatching this click, but stating the invariant explicitly means a
228	                // reader doesn't have to recall that fact to trust onAddToBag can't fire while
229	                // unavailable. Same idiom as ZimmSizeChip's own onClick guard.
230	                if (isUnavailable) return;
231	                onAddToBag?.();
232	              }}
233	            >
234	              <ZimmIcon type="bag" aria-hidden />
235	            </chakra.button>
236	          </chakra.div>
237	        )}
238	      </chakra.div>
239	
240	      {showAttributes && (
241	        <chakra.div __css={styles.attributesRow} data-testid="card-content-attributes">
242	          <chakra.span __css={styles.colourText}>{colourWithComma}</chakra.span>
243	          <chakra.span __css={styles.sizeText}>{size}</chakra.span>
244	        </chakra.div>
245	      )}
246	
247	      <chakra.div __css={styles.priceWrapper} data-card-slot={CARD_SLOT.price}>
248	        <ZimmProductPrice
249	          currentPrice={currentPrice}
250	          originalPrice={originalPrice}
251	          isLoading={isPriceLoading}
252	          isLive={false}
253	        />
254	      </chakra.div>
255	
256	      {showSizeChips && (
257	        <chakra.div __css={styles.sizeChipWrapper} data-card-slot={CARD_SLOT.sizeChips}>
258	          <ZimmSizeChipGroup
259	            values={sizeChipValues ?? []}
260	            selectedValue={selectedSizeChipValue}
261	            onSelect={onSizeChipSelect}
262	          />
263	        </chakra.div>
264	      )}
265	
266	      {showNotifyMeButton && (
267	        <chakra.button
268	          type="button"
269	          __css={styles.notifyMeButton}
270	          onClick={onNotifyMe}
271	          data-card-slot={CARD_SLOT.notifyMe}
272	        >
273	          {intl.formatMessage(messages.notifyMe)}
274	        </chakra.button>
275	      )}
276	    </chakra.div>
277	  );
278	};
279	
280	export default ZimmProductCardContent;
281

import { breakpoints } from 'app/theme/foundation';

/**
 * Shared DOM-contract constants for the ZimmProductCard organism and its composed molecules
 * (ZimmProductCardMedia, ZimmProductCardContent) — defined once here so every producer (the JSX
 * that stamps a `data-card-slot` attribute) and consumer (the organism's own recipe selectors,
 * plus this component family's test suites) reads the same value instead of each independently
 * retyping it. Same pattern, smaller scale, as `zimmColourSwatchGroupShared.ts`.
 */

/**
 * The ten `data-card-slot` attribute values that wire the organism's hover/reveal CSS
 * (`zimmProductCard.css.ts`) to specific descendant DOM nodes. `media` / `badge` / `close` /
 * `carousel` / `indicator` are stamped by `ZimmProductCardMedia`; `content` / `bag` / `price` /
 * `sizeChips` / `notifyMe` by `ZimmProductCardContent`. Do not rename a value here without
 * checking both molecules' own docblocks, which document what each slot is for.
 */
export const CARD_SLOT = {
  media: 'media',
  badge: 'badge',
  close: 'close',
  carousel: 'carousel',
  indicator: 'indicator',
  content: 'content',
  bag: 'bag',
  price: 'price',
  sizeChips: 'sizeChips',
  notifyMe: 'notifyMe',
} as const;

/**
 * Hover-capable-pointer gate shared by every hover-only affordance across the card family
 * (desktop arrows, the hover-reveal price/size-selector swap, the notify-me reveal) — the
 * resolved SFCC-236 decision that arrows and the touch slide-indicator are mutually exclusive by
 * pointer capability, not viewport width.
 */
export const HOVER_CAPABLE_QUERY = '@media (hover: hover) and (pointer: fine)';

/**
 * Desktop viewport-width gate shared by the two places with a real min-width-driven layout
 * change: the organism's own PLP bag-icon mobile hide (`zimmProductCard.css.ts`) and
 * `ZimmProductCardContent`'s responsive outer padding (`zimmProductCardContent.css.ts`).
 * Extracted for the identical reason `HOVER_CAPABLE_QUERY` above was — each file previously
 * derived this independently from the same `breakpoints.md` token, which is exactly the
 * same-value-typed-twice drift risk a shared constant removes.
 */
export const DESKTOP_QUERY = `@media (min-width: ${breakpoints.md})`;
